facts: Lameness in a cow can be associated with hoof problems such as digital dermatitis.
Digital dermatitis is a specific hoof problem causing lesions in cattle.
An udder is defined as a large pendulous organ consisting of two or more mammary glands enclosed in a common envelope, with each provided with a single teat.
The internal anatomy of the mammary gland/udder includes alveoli, lobules containing alveoli, lobes, connective tissue, major ducts, ducts, gland cistern, teat cistern, and teat meatus.
The teat meatus is the terminal opening of the teat canal through which milk exits.
Milk flows from the duct system into the gland cistern, then into the teat cistern, and exits via the teat meatus.

The section titled 'DIGESTIVE PHYSIOLOGY OF RUMINANTS' has two stated objectives: 1. To compare the digestive physiology of ruminants and non-ruminants, and 2. To learn the digestive physiology of ruminants.
A comparative topic introduced on this page is 'Ruminants vs. Non-ruminants'.
